manifest.name: dsh-tool-drawer
manifest.description: On-demand tool groups for DeepSeek Harness: hide heavy tool sets from the context, open them on demand.
manifest.author: kmyy350234-dz

bundle.text:
- insert:
    - id: lazy-tools
      name: dsh-tool-drawer
      config:
        level: medium
        minTools: 3
        groups:
          - id: cua-screen
            match:
              [
                're:^cua_driver_native__(get_|list_|check_permissions|health_report|debug_window_info|clipboard_read|verify_state)'
              ]
            title: 桌面·看
            defaultOn: false
            expect: 19
          - id: cua-input
            match:
              [
                're:^cua_driver_native__(bring_to_front|browser_(click|dialog|download|navigate|pointer|prepare|set_input_files|type)|click|clipboard_write|double_click|drag|end_session|escalate_session|hotkey|install_ffmpeg|invoke_menu|kill_app|launch_app|move_cursor|page|press_key|replay_trajectory|right_click|scroll|set_(agent_cursor_(enabled|motion|theme)|config|value|window_frame)|start_(recording|session)|stop_recording|type_text|zoom)$'
              ]
            title: 桌面·点
            defaultOn: false
            expect: 37
          - id: browser-heavy
            match: [ 're:^dsh_browser_(?!open$|content$|a11y$|click$|type$|wait$)' ]
            keep:
              [
                dsh_browser_open,
                dsh_browser_content,
                dsh_browser_a11y,
                dsh_browser_click,
                dsh_browser_type,
                dsh_browser_wait
              ]
            title: 浏览器·重
            defaultOn: false
            expect: 28
          - id: vision-heavy
            match: [ 're:^vision_(?!describe$|ocr$|crop$|bootstrap$|materialize$|present$)' ]
            keep:
              [
                vision_describe,
                vision_ocr,
                vision_crop,
                vision_bootstrap,
                vision_materialize,
                vision_present
              ]
            title: 视觉·重
            defaultOn: false
            expect: 8

readme.text:
﻿# 工具抽屉 · dsh-tool-drawer

**中文** | [English](README.en.md)

装上两百来个工具之后，问题会变得很明显：模型每一轮都要把这些工具的说明读一遍——哪怕这次只需要改一个错别字。一晚上下来，真正被调用过的工具往往不到一半。

工具抽屉处理的就是这件事：平时用不上的工具组收起来，要用的时候再放出来。

**状态：0.18.x。** 在一台机器上日常使用。配置面仍可能变化。Issue 和 PR 都欢迎，维护是尽力而为；需要稳定保证请自行 fork。DSH 若实现原生按需加载，这个项目应当退场。

实测过的宿主：**DSH 2.0.20-next** 与 **2.0.21-next**（2.0.21 起 `pwsh` 被 `ops_*` 取代；插件不做版本分支，保护清单用两代并集，缺失的名字是空操作）。更早的版本未测。

---

默认行为就是全部，**不需要打开任何设置，也不需要写任何配置**：

- 出厂四组（桌面·看 / 桌面·点 / 浏览器·重 / 视觉·重），按最近使用自动收放；
- 被收起的工具**在你真的调用它的时候会自动放出来**（守卫机制），不用先知道它属于哪一组；
- 需要某个能力时，模型调 `lazy_tools_enable` 把组放回来；它直接调用被收起的工具时，守卫会先放回、再直接执行；
- 想看现状：`lazy_tools_status`；想本会话全开：`lazy_tools_mode { idleDays: 0 }`。

一句话：装上，照常用。

按「从轻到重」排，下面四处都是纯文本：

| 想改什么 | 改哪里 |
|---|---|
| 档位 / 闲置天数 / 是否显示控件 / 分类提示开关 | 设置页，或 `~/.dsh/lazy-tools.policy.json` |
| 有共同前缀的工具组（`dsh_browser_*` 这类） | 包的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里的 `groups`，或配置 `extraGroups`（**追加**，不动默认组） |
| 没有共同前缀的工具（`click` / `type_text` 这种裸名） | `~/.dsh/lazy-tools.groups.json`；也可以让 AI 调 `lazy_tools_save_groups`（不传 `groups` 看描述、带 `groups` 落盘） |
| 只想看不想写 | `lazy_tools_status` / `lazy_tools_list` / `lazy_tools_health` |

匹配式支持 `*` 通配和 `re:` 正则；每组可写 `keep`（永不收起）、`expect`（数量断言）。

**三条红线**（这个项目自己也不越过）：**默认**不在会话中途改工具表（例外只有显式动作 `enable`/`disable`/`mode`/`save_groups{applyNow}` 与自愈补开，且都要留痕）· 自救工具永不入组 · 失败必须报出来。展开在 [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md)。

---

**实测**（2026-10-28，本机 168 个注册工具）：

```
工具定义合计        178,702 字符   # 只算本会话真正相关的（可见 + 收起）
当前收起 48 个       94,792 字符   （53%）
注册表内可见 101 个  83,910 字符
宿主未挂载 19 个     23,637 字符   # 从没进过上下文，不算「省下的」

> 这台机器上有 19 个工具（`cua_driver_native__*`）宿主压根没挂到会话里 —— 它们从没花过 token，所以**单列**，不并进「省下了多少」。工具全部挂载的机器上这一项为 0，数字会回到「收起 67 个 / 118,429 字符 / 58%」。
> **缓存账（2026-10-30 补）**：上面报的是「工具 schema 不进请求」省下的**字符数**，不是账单上的等比值。
> 稳态下工具定义本来就在前缀缓存里命中，命中价通常只有未命中的几分之一（具体倍率由服务商决定，这里不编数字）；
> 而**会话中途改工具表**会让后续请求的缓存作废一次 —— 本插件会中途改表的只有：自愈、显式 `enable`/`disable`/`mode`、`save_groups {applyNow:true}`。
> 它们都是「用户或模型当下就要用」，不是优化手段；如果一次会话都没触发，缓存一次都不会被打断。
> **这组数是「冷启动 / 还没用热」时的实测**：用久了，热组会默认开着，收起量自然往下走 —— 那不是虚报，是插件的设计（按使用热度）。复现请跑 `lazy_tools_health { bench: true }`。
> 另有 34 个**不在工具注册表里**的工具：33 个宿主内核（`read` / `write` / `pwsh` / `glob` / `web_fetch` …）+ 1 个 agent 作用域的 `ops_discover_tools` —— 它们不进注册表，也不上表统计，不会被收起。

换算成 token 请用你自己 provider 的 tokenizer —— 这里只报**字符数**，因为不同语言的描述密度差别很大，硬编一个系数等于替读者猜。

**这个数字随时可以自己复现**：

```
lazy_tools_health { bench: true }
```

它会把每个组的工具数、收起的字符数、可见/收起/未挂载三态都列出来（百分比自己除一下）。README 里所有数字都来自这条命令。

> 早期版本写的是「约 220 token/工具」的估算；换成 `lazy_tools_health { bench: true }` 之后，改成实测字符数，读者可以核对。

DSH 的工具注册表支持按 agent 隐藏全局工具，接口是 `restrict({ deny: [...] })`。

每个 agent 创建时，把配置组内的工具填进 `deny`，它们就从模型可见的工具表里消失；解除这条限制即恢复。

整个过程不引入：

- 代理进程（调用不经过中间层）；
- 向量检索（不额外跑模型判断意图）；
- 包装器（真实调用仍是原生调用，参数校验不变）。

不用向量路由的原因：路由错一次，需要的工具会被静默藏掉，模型只会回「没有这个能力」；另外为省 token 引入一个 90MB 编码器并不划算。

这是一个 bundle：宿主半边加一个设置页的客户端半边。三种装法，任选其一。

**从 GitHub 直接装（插件市场显示的就是这条）：**

```
dsh plugin --profile web add github:kmyy350234-dz/dsh-tool-drawer
```

**或者用仓库里的 Release 包（不依赖 npm）：**

```
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/kmyy350234-dz/dsh-tool-drawer/releases/latest/download/dsh-tool-drawer.tgz
```

**或者 clone 到任意位置，用插件管理器装：**

```
plugin_manager install_bundle  target: /你的路径/dsh-tool-drawer
```

不建议手改 `cordis.patch.yml`——手写也能运行，但只有宿主半边，**没有设置页**。

bundle 自带的 patch 已配好四组：

| 组 | 收起数量 | 保留（永不收起） |
|---|---|---|
| 桌面·看 | 19 | 无 |
| 桌面·点 | 37 | 无 |
| 浏览器·重 | 28 | open / content / a11y / click / type / wait |
| 视觉·重 | 8 | describe / ocr / crop / bootstrap / materialize / present |

改组成员改 checkout 里的 `cordis.patch.yml`。配置改动重载生效；**改宿主代码需要重启进程**。

插件越装越多，新插件带进来的工具没人管，就一直可见、一直付 token。`autoGroups` 让插件按**工具名前缀**识别家族，自动给它们建组。

插件目录的收录描述里提醒过：自带分组只覆盖 `cua_driver_native` / `dsh_browser` / `vision` 三类，其他工具要在 `cordis.patch.yml` 里自己加。**`autoGroups` 补的就是这一步**——其余家族会被自动识别成组；想改匹配式或加 `keep` 名单，再回去写配置。

| 模式 | 行为 |
|---|---|
| `off` | 完全不动 |
| `suggest` | 只在 `lazy_tools_list { ungrouped: true }` 的 `autoGroups.suggestions` 里给建议，不建组 |
| `on`（默认） | 自动建组，并按规则默认收起。被收起的工具第一次被调用时会自动放回来，所以「误分组」最多多一次往返 |

**新装的插件可能被自动收起**：自动组的 id 以 `auto-` 开头（如 `auto-foo`），用 `lazy_tools_disable auto-foo` 就能解散；核心工具永不入组；被收起的工具第一次被调用时，守卫会自动把它放回来。

规则都写死在代码里，不靠猜：

- 按 `__` 或 `_` 切段；**子族合计覆盖 ≥80% 才往下切**，否则保留整族（`mnemon` 的 17 个不会被切成两个 3 个）；
- 同一前缀 ≥ `minTools`（默认 3）个才建组；
- 已被现有组覆盖 ≥80% 的前缀跳过；
- **核心工具永不入组**（`read` / `write` / `edit` / `pwsh` / `grep` / `glob` / `skill` / `todo_write` / `lazy_tools_*` 等）；
- 只在会话开始时算一次，整场不变（不打断前缀缓存）；
- 自动组 id 带 `auto-` 前缀，`lazy_tools_status` 里看得见，`lazy_tools_disable auto-xxx` 一条命令解散。

**看不到内核内置工具**：`read`、`schedule`、`job` 这类不在插件注册表里，自动分组不会碰它们。

想自定义匹配式或 keep 名单，仍然写配置——下一节。

| 字段 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `id` | 组 id，工具调用时使用 |
| `match` | 匹配式数组。普通字符串按 glob 处理（`*` 通配、整串锚定）；`re:` 开头按正则处理 |
| `keep` | 有意保留可见的工具名，不会被判定为「漏网」 |
| `expect` | 该组**至少**应有的工具数量（下限）；**少于**它时 `health` 告警，多出来不算漂移（吸纳型组本来就会长新工具） |
| `defaultOn` | `false` 表示默认收起 |
| `title` | 供 `status` 展示的中文名 |

> **它做什么、不做什么**：受管角色是在**编排器已经给出的工具集上再收紧**。`restrict` 在作用域链上取交集，
> 所以它**不能给角色加上编排器没给的工具**——worker 没有浏览器工具，抽屉变不出来。
> 它防的是「角色会话里冒出不该有的工具」，不是「给角色分配能力」。

多会话编排器（如 dsh-superagent）用 preset 区分角色。默认情况下本插件不区分角色，所有会话都按热度判断。配置 `managedRoles` 后，某个 preset 会被认成「受管角色」：策略在会话创建时解析一次，会话内不变（前缀稳定、不打断缓存）。

**写在哪**：`~/.dsh/lazy-tools.policy.json` 的 `managedRoles` 字段（**JSON**，不是 YAML；和设置页那些档位存在同一个文件），或者插件的 config（profile 里的 YAML）。两处都有时以 policy.json 为准。

```json
{
  "managedRoles": {
    "dsh-superagent-worker": { "allowGroups": ["cua-screen", "browser-heavy"] },
    "dsh-superagent-router": { "allowGroups": ["cua-screen"] },

> **组 id 必须是这台机器上真实存在的**：默认四组是 `cua-screen` / `cua-input` / `browser-heavy` / `vision-heavy`，
> 另有你手写组的 id、以及自动分组生成的 `auto-<前缀>`。不确定就先跑 `lazy_tools_status` 看 `groups[].id`。

规则：

- 只认结构信号：`agentPresets.composedPreset` 的 preset id，以及 `session.header.parentSession`（子代理 → `subagent` 键）；不认插件名、不认标题；
- **封闭默认**：角色没授权的组、以及没有归组的工具，一律隐藏（`unknown: 'hide'`）；
- 受管会话里 `enable` / `disable` 会被拒绝，自愈也不会绕过策略——改策略请改配置；
- **写错组 id 会被抓出来**（2026-11-02 加）：启动时校验 `allowGroups`，`health.errors` 会写明「哪个角色的哪些 id 不存在」。
  如果某个角色的组**全都不存在**，这个角色**不生效**（退回普通会话行为）——否则受管会话里既不能 `enable`、自愈也不绕过，
  就等于把一个会话锁到只剩核心工具，还全程静默；
- `allowGroups: ["*"]` 表示这个角色不按组设限（逃生口）；
- `allowGroups: []` 表示**只留常驻工具（CORE）**，其余全部收起（2026-11-05 起合法）；
- `health` 新增 `managed: { role, allowGroups, unknown }`，没有受管就是 `null`；
- 不配置 `managedRoles` 时行为与旧版完全一致（默认关闭）。

测试：冒烟 `[61]` 覆盖 worker / subagent / 普通会话三条路径与 enable 拒绝；`[71]` 覆盖「组 id 写错」的三种情况
（全错停用、半错照用、`*` 放行）。

readme.section: 给子代理分角色：只认宿主给的信号，不做文本约定（2026-11-03）
readme.text:
给子代理分角色，走的是**宿主原生信号**，不引入我们自己的提示词协议：

1. **会话 label**（首选）——编排器给子会话打 `vendor:role` 这类标签时，取候选段挑 `managedRoles` 里配过的；
2. `subagent` 通用键——任何用 `subagent` 派工的场景；
3. preset id——一角色一 preset 的场景。

> **为什么不做 `[role:xxx]` 这种文本标记**（0.18.1 短暂有过、0.18.2 删除）：
> 它要求「派工的人」改提示词才能生效，而多数编排器的 label 里本来就没有角色词——
> 两个通道解决的是同一件事，多一个私有协议只会多一套行为要解释。
> 0.17.0 立过一条红线：**不再监听 inbox 消息**。那条红线现在恢复。

生态里各家给子会话打「角色」的写法不同，我们**不认厂商名**，只按顺序试这**三**种，**每一种都要求 `managedRoles` 里配过那个键**：

| 顺序 | 信号 | 例子 | `health.managed.source` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **会话标签里的候选段**（按 `:` `/` `|` 空白切开，逐段小写，**挑 `managedRoles` 里配过的那个**） | `dsh-my-go:hermes: 帮我改模块` → `hermes` | `label` |
| 2 | 子会话通用键 | 任意子代理 | `subagent` |
| 3 | preset id | `cordis` / 自定义 preset | `preset` |

- 标签只在**子会话**上认（`header.parentSession`）；普通会话的标签不生效。
- 认不出 / 没配 ⇒ 不做任何事（失败方向放开）。**`[role:xxx]` 提示词标记已删除**（0.18.2）：写了也不会生效，也不会报错。
- 所以 MyGO（真实标签是 `dsh-my-go:<工种>: <任务摘要>`，见它 `preset/shared/misc.mjs` 的 `agentLabel`）这类编排器**不用改一行代码**就能对接；
- ⚠️ 但**配置的键要写工种名本身**（`hermes`），不要写 `dsh-my-go:hermes` —— 前缀只是标签的一部分，不是角色名。

测试：冒烟 `[74]`。

角色 → 组的映射由 **AI 自己配**：`lazy_tools_roles`（不传参数=只读；传 `role + allowGroups + basis`=写入）。

```text
lazy_tools_roles({ role: "hermes", allowGroups: ["write"], basis: "写模块，不碰浏览器" })
→ 写进 policy.json，带 createdBy: "ai" + at + basis → 下一个会话立即生效（不用重启）
```

工具层强制三条不变量（人手写 JSON 可以绕过，AI 不行）：

| 不变量 | 原因 |
|---|---|
| 组 id 必须真实存在 | 写错一个就是"会话被锁到只剩核心工具"（`#71`） |
| **不许写 `*`** | `*` 是放开限制的逃生口，**只允许人手改文件** |
| 必须带 `basis` | 让"为什么这么配"留在记录里，权限不是一个凭空的决定 |

- **喜欢折腾的人**：直接改 `policy.json` 的 `managedRoles`（可以写 `*`、可以不带 basis）——**改完不用重启**，下一个会话生效；
- `health.managed` 显示 `createdBy` / `basis`，一眼看出这个角色是谁配的、为什么；
- 受管会话里不能给自己改配置（否则"角色"就管不住自己了）。

测试：冒烟 `[75]`（热重载）、`[76]`（三条不变量 + 写入即生效）。

常驻提示里列出的组，按**每个会话实际挂载的工具**算，不是一张全局固定清单：

- 挂载集 = 本会话可见的工具 ∪ 本插件自己藏起来的工具，只列其中有成员的组；
- **一组都没挂载时整段提示消失**（宿主会丢掉空段）——不会再出现「目录里列着一个这个会话根本碰不到的组」；
- 被外部挡掉的（宿主的权限门、别的插件的 deny）**不算挂载**，不会被广告；
- 「有 N 个工具没归组、去分组」这句提醒只在**默认 preset 的人工会话**里出现，角色会话不会被引导去改全局分组表；
- 读不到会话信息（老宿主、服务缺失、认不出的作用域）时**退回 0.17.x 行为**：照旧列全部组。失败方向是「照旧」，不是「变短」。

测试：冒烟 `[64]`（没挂 / 被外部挡的组不广告、空则空段、认不出作用域退回旧行为）与
`[65]`（分类提示只在默认会话出现）。

| 工具 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `lazy_tools_status` | 查看每组状态：开关、模式、匹配数量、可见数量、是否热、上次使用时间 |
| `lazy_tools_enable` | 打开一组；`only: ['名字']` 只放指定工具；`groups: [...]` 批量打开；**`name: '工具名'` 按名字一步开一个**（原 resolve） |
| `lazy_tools_disable` | 收起一组，同时清除 `only` 白名单 |
| `lazy_tools_list` | 列出组内工具（含被隐藏的）；`ungrouped: true` 附带前缀分桶 + 未归组工具的描述（原 scan / classify） |
| `lazy_tools_mode` | 仅修改当前会话策略；`reset` 回全局，`collapse` 立即清空 |
| `lazy_tools_health` | 自检五个宿主契约，输出 warnings / 漏网工具 / 自愈次数；**`bench: true` 附带基准账**（注册总数、可见/收起、每组字符数 —— README 数字的唯一来源） |
| `lazy_tools_save_groups` | 把分好的组写进 `~/.dsh/lazy-tools.groups.json`；默认下次会话生效，`applyNow: true` 才立刻生效 |
| `lazy_tools_roles` | 查看/配置「角色 → 允许哪些组」；写入后即时生效（AI 自配会带 `createdBy` / `basis`，可追溯） |
`healthy: true` 表示：五个契约均通过（register / schemas / restrict / guard / agent 事件），无错误（宿主销毁竞态除外，那条只留证据不拉红灯），无警告。

设置页由客户端半边渲染，通过**本机回环路由**（`127.0.0.1`）与宿主半边通信，不连任何外部地址。

> 2026-11-05 起，这条路由的 **Host 必须是回环**（`127.0.0.1` / `localhost` / `[::1]`）；用反代或局域网机器名访问设置页会被 403。要那样用，请在反代上把 Host 改写成回环。插件市场的能力扫描把这类调用标成「会联网」，指的是这一次本机 HTTP 调用，不是外网上传。

宿主默认**只监听 `127.0.0.1`**（2026-10-29 实测：DSH 的 web 服务在 `127.0.0.1` 上，同一进程没有任何 `0.0.0.0` 监听）。所以这条桥**不需要再做一层鉴权**——加 token 属于「为回环工具新造一个部件」，按本项目红线不成立。若哪天宿主改成监听 `0.0.0.0`，那是宿主配置问题，应改监听地址，而不是在本插件里造鉴权层。

`lib/config.js` 导出 schema，DSH 设置页据此渲染字段：

| 字段 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `level` | `medium` | 收敛力度：低 14 天、中 7 天、高 3 天 |
| `presets` | `{14,7,3}` | 三档各自的天数，可修改 |
| `idleDays` | 跟随 `level` | 手动指定天数；0 表示不按时间收敛 |
| `minTools` | `3` | **自动分组**的建组门槛：同前缀少于 3 个不建组（下限 3，填更小也按 3 跑） |
| `showDock` | `false` | 在输入框上方显示档位按钮 |
| `showClear` | `false` | 在输入框上方显示独立的「立刻清空」按钮 |
| `classifyNudge` | `true` | 有裸名工具没归组时，在常驻提示里提醒模型分类（一次，落盘后长期生效） |
| `autoGroups` | `on` | 自动分组：`off` / `suggest` / `on` |

两个界面开关互相独立。控件按对话挂载，勾选后需切换一次对话（或刷新页面）才会出现。

组定义保留在 bundle 的 patch 中：写一次后很少改动，且嵌套数组在表单中可读性差。

schema 在运行时解析：扫描 `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\*\` 查找 DSH 自带的 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`，只使用 Node 内置模块。未找到时 `Config` 为 undefined——没有设置页，插件本身正常运行。

设置页写入的策略保存在 `~/.dsh/lazy-tools.policy.json`，优先级高于 YAML 默认值；删除该文件即回到默认。

readme.section: 为什么它表现得像会自己判断
readme.text:
它不判断，只按证据触发。两个机制都不包含猜测：

**一、用量账本。** 每次真实调用记录一条时间戳到 `~/.dsh/lazy-tools.usage.json`（只记时间与工具名，不记参数）。新会话开始时计算：**组内热工具占比**达到 `warmRatio`（默认 30%）才整组打开；没到阈值只放「热的那几个」（`only`）；一个都不热才整组收起。组级时间戳只用于展示 `lastUsed`，不参与决策（2026-10-30 改）。

该决策**默认只在会话开始时执行一次**。原因：中途修改工具表会使前缀缓存失效，省下的 token 不足以抵消损失。**被允许的例外**只有显式动作（`enable`/`disable`/`mode`/`save_groups{applyNow}`）与自愈补开（模型已经叫错了名字，不补就白花一轮）。

**二、自愈。** 当模型调用被隐藏的工具时，一个 dispatch 守卫会在拒绝之前拦截：识别所属组，只放出该工具，**然后直接放行这一次调用**（2026-11-05 起；以前是返回「请重试」，在 UI 上会显示成一次假失败）。

readme.section: 为什么它表现得像会自己判断
readme.text: 补开后直接执行，用户侧无感知。次数记录在 `health.stats.selfHealed`。

**漏网工具。** 插件升级新增工具而组匹配式未覆盖时，该工具会重新变为可见并持续占用 token。`health.stray` 会推导每组的名字前缀，列出「看起来属于该族、但未被任何组匹配」的可见工具（`keep` 中的除外）。

**数量漂移。** 每组配置 `expect`（**下限**）；工具数**少于**它时 `health` 告警 —— 多出来是吸纳型组的正常状态，不报。

**客户端没挂上。** `health.client` 记录浏览器那半边最后一次上报（`seen` / `at` / `agoSeconds` / 挂了哪些面板）。宿主一切正常**不等于**设置页挂上了：2026-10-24 就出现过「宿主四项契约全绿、客户端条目加载失败、Web 进恢复模式」的情况，这个字段把那类问题从「只能靠重启发现」变成一条能查的数据。

**竞态。** 子 agent 可能在限制建立过程中被销毁；这类失败只计入 `stats.restrictSkipped`，**不进 `errors`**（否则多会话场景会把错误槽占满）。

**孤儿限制。** 解除函数挂在 `ctx.effect` 上，热重载会解除它们。
但 `own()` 目前是**先置位 done、再调 dispose**：如果 dispose 抛错，后续 lift 与热重载都不会再试（已知问题，票 `lift-orphan-done-before-dispose` 修）。

```
node test/smoke.mjs
```

以 `node test/smoke.mjs` 的输出为准（项数以实际输出为准，不写死），运行在假宿主上，不需要安装 DSH。

假宿主实现本插件依赖的四个**契约**（register / schemas / restrict / agent-created），外加宿主那条**可选**的
`tools.view(scope)` 只读视图（提示段的主读路径就是它；视图缺失、返回空、抛错三种退化都有用例钉住）。
宿主契约变化时，测试先失败，而不是会话先出问题。

> 要改这个插件？先读 [MAINTAINING.md](MAINTAINING.md)：改客户端半边必须冷启动验证，恢复模式下用户无法操作。

1. **只能隐藏全局工具。** 注册在 agent 作用域中的工具无法隐藏，宿主会拒绝。
   若一批里混进这种名字，插件会**逐个重试**：能藏的照藏，藏不掉的记一条并跳过（不再让整批失效）。
2. **按名字分组。** DSH 的工具定义没有标签，只能对名字写 glob 或正则；改名会导致漏配。
3. **开关会打断前缀缓存。** 打开一次后尽量保持；需要反复切换时优先使用 `only:`，不要整组开关。
4. **自动收敛只在会话开始。** 运行期间不重排，理由同上。
5. **失败方向是放开。** 契约异常或文件不可读时，工具全部回到可见状态：多花 token，但不会减少能力。
6. **自愈只对「存在但被隐藏」的工具有效。** 拼写错误、尚未加载的插件无法修复，这类情况用 `lazy_tools_enable { name: '片段' }` 按片段查找（原 `resolve`，0.16.0 并入）。
7. **界面双语，工具描述不是。** 设置面板和输入框那一行跟随宿主语言服务；模型读取的工具描述在启动时注册一次，仍为中文——宿主进程无法感知界面语言。
DSH 已带有 `deferLoading` 与工具增补消息。若其实现原生按需加载，这个项目应当退场，而不是继续并行维护。

| 项目 | 做法 | 取舍 |
|---|---|---|
| [tool-attention](https://github.com/asadani/tool-attention)（[论文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21816)） | 每轮基于 embedding 的意图路由，两段式加载 schema | 量化了「工具税」；未采用 embedding，因为路由错误会静默隐藏所需工具 |
| [mcp-lazy-load](https://github.com/PeterCha90/mcp-lazy-load) | MCP 代理，暴露 `search_tools` / `execute_tool` | 证明可大幅缩减；选择保持原生调用，不经过通用执行器 |
| [dsh-mcp-loader](https://github.com/MikotoMyWife/dsh-mcp-loader) | DSH 插件，按服务器加载并对 agent 施加 `restrict` 掩码 | 同一机制层；本实现不绑定命名空间，并增加 `only:` |
| [lazy-mcp](https://github.com/voicetreelab/lazy-mcp) | 代理层，按服务器分树 | 分组词汇参考 |
| [opencode-lazy-loading](https://github.com/omarwaly-ai/opencode-lazy-loading) | 请求层剥离 | 大幅缩减说法的参考 |
| [dsh-sieve](https://github.com/Sev7eEn7/dsh-sieve) | DSH 上下文过滤，带裁判模型 | 避免「模型在环」判断的理由 |
| [microsoft/agent-framework 的 progressive disclosure 示例](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/blob/e39a8a2e/python/samples/02-agents/mcp/mcp_progressive_disclosure.py) | 按需暴露 MCP 工具 | 术语参考 |
若相关作者认为描述有误，可开 Issue 指正。

- **不是代理、网关或 MCP 客户端。** 不接触传输层，不增加跳跃。
- **不是自动路由。** 不猜测用户意图，仅在明确请求时打开。
- **不是安全边界。** 隐藏只是从模型列表中移除，不阻止执行；权限控制请使用宿主机制。

MIT，见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。

---

Tool Drawer for DeepSeek Harness: keeps heavy tool groups out of every request and restores them on
demand (one call, a dispatch guard that reopens it, or an on-demand enable). The numbers are measured, not estimated — see the
table above (that table is the **only** place these figures live). No proxy, no embeddings, no judge model — real calls stay
native. Install with `plugin_manager install_bundle`; configure in the DSH settings page. MIT,
best-effort maintenance.

﻿# Tool Drawer · dsh-tool-drawer

[中文](README.md) | **English**

> You installed a pile of plugins; the tool list keeps growing, and every request pays tokens for
> tools this task will never touch. **Tool Drawer** keeps heavy groups collapsed, leaves the ones you
> actually use on the bench, lets stale ones sink on their own — and brings a tool back with one call,
> a guard that catches a real call and reopens it, or an explicit `lazy_tools_enable`.

**Status:** `0.17.x` — used daily on one DSH installation; the config surface may still change.

Tested hosts: **DSH 2.0.20-next** and **2.0.21-next** (2.0.21 replaced `pwsh` with `ops_*`; the plugin does not branch on versions — the protected list is the union of both generations, and names a host does not have are no-ops).
Issues and PRs are welcome, but maintenance is **best-effort**. If DSH ships native on-demand tool
loading, this project should retire (see *Exit criteria*).

---
The defaults are the whole feature set. **No settings page, no config file, nothing to write:**
Install it, keep working.

readme.section: If you want to tune it
readme.text:
| What you want | Where to change it |
|---|---|
| Level / idle days / dock visibility / classification nudge | the settings page, or `~/.dsh/lazy-tools.policy.json` |
| Groups for tools with a shared prefix (`dsh_browser_*` …) | `groups` in the package `cordis.patch.yml`, or config `extraGroups` (**appends**, never replaces the defaults) |
| Tools with no shared prefix (`click`, `type_text` …) | `~/.dsh/lazy-tools.groups.json`; or let the agent call `lazy_tools_save_groups` (no `groups` = classification material, with `groups` = write) |
| Read-only inspection | `lazy_tools_status` / `lazy_tools_list` / `lazy_tools_health` |
| `lazy_tools_list { ungrouped: true }` | Lists ungrouped tools with descriptions plus name-prefix buckets (absorbs the old `scan` / `classify`) |
| `lazy_tools_save_groups` | Writes the chosen groups to `~/.dsh/lazy-tools.groups.json`; takes effect next session unless `applyNow: true` |

readme.section: If you want to tune it
readme.text:
Match patterns accept `*` globs and `re:` regexes; each group may carry `keep` (never collapse) and `expect` (lower bound on member count).

**Three red lines** (this project holds itself to them too): do **not** change the tool table mid-session by default (exceptions: explicit `enable`/`disable`/`mode`/`save_groups { applyNow: true }`, and self-heal — all logged) · recovery tools never go into a group · failures must be reported. Details in [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

---

**Measured** (2026-10-28, 168 registered tools on one machine):

```
all tool definitions   178,702 chars   # visible-in-registry + collapsed (this session's scope)
collapsed (48 tools)    94,792 chars   (53%)
visible in registry (101)   83,910 chars
not mounted (19 tools)  23,637 chars   # never entered context — not counted as savings

> 19 tools here (`cua_driver_native__*`) are never mounted into the session by the host, so they
> never cost a token; they are listed separately instead of being folded into "how much it saves".
> On a machine where every tool mounts, that row is 0 and the figures become
> "collapsed 67 / 118,429 chars / 58%".
> Another 34 tools live **outside the tool registry**: 33 host core tools (`read` / `write` / `pwsh` /
> `glob` / `web_fetch`, …) plus 1 agent-scoped `ops_discover_tools`. They are outside this table and are
> never collapsed.

Convert to tokens with your own provider's tokenizer — only character counts are reported here, because description density differs too much between languages for a fixed ratio to be honest.

Reproduce it anytime with `lazy_tools_health { bench: true }`; every number in this README comes from that command.

> **Cache accounting:** the numbers above are **characters of tool definitions**, not a matching discount on your bill. In steady state tool schemas are served from the prefix cache, which usually costs a fraction of a miss (the exact ratio is provider-specific — this project does not invent one). Changing the tool table **mid-session** invalidates that cache once; this plugin only does so when the user or the model needs a tool *right now* (self-heal, or explicit enable/disable/mode/save_groups { applyNow: true }).

Every tool schema is tokens in *every* request. A desktop-automation plugin can carry 50+ tools, a
browser plugin 30+, a vision plugin a dozen — hundreds of definitions the model reads on each turn,
even when the task never needs them.

The numbers are measured, not estimated — see the table above, which is the **only** place these figures
live. It also explains the one caveat: 19 tools this host never mounts are counted separately,
and a machine where everything mounts collapses 67.
**These are cold-start / not-yet-warmed numbers.** Over time, groups that get used stay open by design,
so the collapsed count drifts down — that is the heat model working, not a doctored figure. Re-run
`lazy_tools_health { bench: true }` to reproduce.

readme.section: How it differs from a proxy or an embedding router
readme.text:
| Approach | What it costs |
|---|---|
| MCP proxy (`search_tools` + `execute_tool`) | every real call goes through a generic wrapper — you lose the native schema validation of arguments |
| Embedding router (intent → tool) | ~90 MB encoder, one retrieval per turn, and a mis-route silently hides the tool you needed |
| **This plugin** | one `restrict({deny})` call on the agent's own scope — no process, no extra hop, no model, no third-party package (the only import is the host's own `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, used to render the settings form, resolved at runtime and optional) |

readme.section: How it differs from a proxy or an embedding router
readme.text:
The trick is simply **gating at the registry-scope layer instead of at the transport or
serialization layer**. If your host exposes a per-agent "hide these global tools" primitive, use it.
Details and trade-offs: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

This package is a **bundle** (host half + a `settings.section` client panel). Three ways to install,
pick one — and do not hand-edit `cordis.patch.yml`:

**Straight from GitHub (the command the plugin directory shows):**

```
dsh plugin --profile web add github:kmyy350234-dz/dsh-tool-drawer
```

**Or use the prebuilt tarball attached to the release (no npm account needed):**

```
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/kmyy350234-dz/dsh-tool-drawer/releases/latest/download/dsh-tool-drawer.tgz
```

**Or clone it anywhere and install with the plugin manager:**

```
plugin_manager install_bundle  target: /absolute/path/to/dsh-tool-drawer
```

That links the checkout into the profile, selects the bundle, and starts the client half. The bundle
patch already ships four groups (`cua-screen` 19, `cua-input` 37, `browser-heavy` 28, `vision-heavy` 8);
only the latter two carry `keep` lists. Edit `cordis.patch.yml` in the
checkout (or override the row in the profile patch) to change members.

Config changes apply on reload; **host code changes need a process restart**. The settings page is
drawn by the client half and talks to the host over a loopback route.

The more plugins you install, the more unmanaged tools appear and keep paying tokens every request.
`autoGroups` recognises tool families by **name prefix** and groups them for you:

The directory listing notes that the shipped groups only cover `cua_driver_native` / `dsh_browser` /
`vision`, and that every other family has to be added by hand. **`autoGroups` closes exactly that
gap**: the remaining families are recognised and grouped for you — drop back to the config only when
you want to change the pattern or add a `keep` list.

| Mode | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `off` | Do nothing |
| `suggest` | Only report suggestions under `autoGroups.suggestions` in `lazy_tools_list { ungrouped: true }`; create nothing |
| `on` (default) | Create the groups and collapse them by the usual rules. A collapsed tool is restored automatically the first time it is called, so a mis-grouped family costs one extra round-trip at worst |

**A newly installed plugin may be auto-collapsed**: auto groups have ids starting with `auto-`
(e.g. `auto-foo`); `lazy_tools_disable auto-foo` dissolves one. Core tools are never included, and a
collapsed tool is restored by the guard the first time it is called.

The rules are fixed in code, not guessed:

**Built-in tools are out of scope**: `read`, `schedule`, `job` and friends are not in the plugin
registry, so auto grouping never touches them.

Custom match patterns or `keep` lists still go in the config — see the next section.

A manual `cordis.patch.yml` row is still possible (see
[profile-patch.snippet.yml](profile-patch.snippet.yml)) but it gets you only the
host half — no settings page.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | group id, used by every tool call |
| `match` | array of patterns. Plain strings are globs (`*` wildcard, anchored); prefix `re:` for a raw regular expression |
| `keep` | tool names that must never be treated as "stray" — the ones you deliberately leave visible |
| `expect` | **lower bound** on the group size; only `matched < expect` produces a `warnings[]` entry (absorbing match patterns grow, and that is fine) |
| `defaultOn` | `false` = hidden unless enabled (almost always what you want) |
| `title` | free-form label shown by `lazy_tools_status` |

> **It only narrows.** `restrict` intersects along the scope chain, so a managed role can never *add* tools the
> orchestrator did not grant — it only removes tools a role session should not see.

Set `managedRoles` in `~/.dsh/lazy-tools.policy.json` (**JSON**, same file as the saved policy), or in the
plugin config (profile YAML); the policy file wins when both exist.

- Group ids must exist on this machine — check `lazy_tools_status` → `groups[].id`.
- Unknown ids are reported in `health.errors`; a role whose ids are **all** unknown is disabled instead of
  locking that session down to CORE tools (managed sessions reject `enable`/`disable`, and self-heal does not
  bypass the policy, so a wrong config would otherwise have no escape inside the session).
- `allowGroups: ["*"]` disables group filtering for that role.
- Without `managedRoles` nothing changes.

readme.section: Per-subagent roles: from the session label (2026-11-03)
readme.text:
The host's `subagent` tool takes no preset or metadata, so every subagent inherits its parent's preset —
preset-based role filtering never distinguishes them (measured: two differently-labelled subagents got identical surfaces).

Three signals are tried in order, and **each one must be configured in `managedRoles`**:

readme.section: Per-subagent roles: from the session label (2026-11-03)
readme.text:
1. **A candidate segment of the session label** — split on `:` `/` `|` and whitespace, lowercase, then take the first
   segment that is a key in `managedRoles` (an exact match beats the trailing summary words). Example:
   `dsh-my-go:hermes: fix the parser` resolves to `hermes`.
2. The generic `subagent` key.
3. The preset id.

```json
{ "managedRoles": { "researcher": { "allowGroups": ["browser-heavy", "vision-heavy"] } } }
```

readme.section: Per-subagent roles: from the session label (2026-11-03)
readme.text:
Only subagent sessions are affected (a label on your own session changes nothing), and an unconfigured role does
nothing at all — no key, no change. The short-lived `[role:xxx]` prompt marker was **removed in 0.18.2**: writing it
has no effect and records no error.
The resident prompt lists the groups the **calling session** actually has mounted, not a fixed global list:
Tests: smoke `[64]` (filtering / empty section / unresolved scope falls back) and `[65]` (nudge only in default sessions).

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `lazy_tools_status` | per group: `on`, `mode` (`hide`/`only`/`all`), `matched`, `visible`, `onlyCount`, `expect`/`expectOk`, `hot`, `lastUsed` |
| `lazy_tools_enable {group \| groups, only?, name?}` | show a group; `only: ['name']` shows exactly those tools; `groups: [...]` for batches; **`name: '<tool or fragment>'` reveals just that one tool** (absorbs the old `resolve`) |
| `lazy_tools_disable {group \| groups}` | hide it again (clears any `only` allow-list) |
| `lazy_tools_list {group?, ungrouped?}` | tool names in a group, including hidden ones; `ungrouped: true` adds ungrouped tools with descriptions plus name-prefix buckets and `autoGroups` suggestions (absorbs the old `scan` / `classify`) |
| `lazy_tools_mode {level?, idleDays?, reset?, collapse?}` | **this session only**: change the threshold and recompute which groups start open (`reset` → global policy, `collapse` → clear this conversation) |
| `lazy_tools_health {tool?, layersFor?, bench?, full?}` | contract self-check; default is a **slim view** (`healthy`, per-group state, `warnings`, `stray`, `client`, `stats`); `{ full: true }` adds ledger `usage`, `contracts[].detail`, `nameProbe
`healthy: true` means: five contracts OK **and** no errors (host dispose races excepted — they stay as evidence) **and** no warnings.

The settings page is drawn by the client half and talks to the host half over a **loopback route**
(`127.0.0.1`); it never connects to an external address. The plugin directory's capability scan
labels such calls as "connects to servers" — that label refers to this local HTTP call, not to any
upload.

`lib/config.js` exports a `Config` schema, so DSH renders these fields in its own settings page:

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `level` | `medium` | collapse aggressiveness: `low` 14 d / `medium` 7 d / `high` 3 d |
| `presets` | `{14,7,3}` | days per level — change them to your own pace |
| `idleDays` | follows `level` | override the day threshold (`0` = never collapse by time) |
| `minTools` | `3` | **auto-grouping** threshold: a prefix needs at least this many tools to become a group (floor 3 — smaller values are clamped) |
| `showDock` | `false` | show the level control above the composer |
| `showClear` | `false` | show the independent "clear now" button above the composer |
| `classifyNudge` | `true` | when bare-named tools have no group, remind the model once in the system prompt to classify them |
| `autoGroups` | `on` | automatic grouping: `off` / `suggest` / `on` |

Both composer toggles are independent; the drawer control is mounted per conversation, so it appears
after switching conversations (or reloading). The panel is bilingual and follows the host locale
service.

Group definitions stay in the bundle patch — written once, rarely touched. The schema is resolved at
runtime by scanning `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\*\` for `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` (a package DSH
already ships), using Node built-ins only; if it can't be found, `Config` is `undefined` — **no
settings page, plugin unaffected**. The panel writes `~/.dsh/lazy-tools.policy.json`, which overrides
the YAML defaults; delete that file to fall back.

readme.section: Why it *feels* automatic (without a model in the loop)
readme.text:
Most people install a pile of plugins and use each of them rarely — but when the moment comes, the
tool has to be there. Two deterministic mechanisms cover that, and none of them guesses:

readme.section: Why it *feels* automatic (without a model in the loop)
readme.text:
0. **Usage ledger + session-start decision** — every real call is recorded in
   `~/.dsh/lazy-tools.usage.json` (timestamps only). When a session starts, a group opens fully when
   the share of its tools used within `idleDays` reaches `warmRatio` (default 0.30); below that only
   those warm tools are revealed (`only`); with none warm the group starts collapsed. Group-level
   timestamps are display-only (`lastUsed`) and no longer drive the decision. The decision happens
   **once, at the session boundary**, so it never invalidates an active prompt cache.
1. **Self-heal / `lazy_tools_enable { name }`** — on an `unknown tool` error, `enable { name }` finds the
   owning group and reveals just that tool; a dispatch guard also tries to reveal it *before* the call is
   rejected, and the call proceeds immediately (only the guard bumps `stats.selfHealed`; `enable { name }` is not counted). The old `resolve` is now this entry point.

readme.section: Why it *feels* automatic (without a model in the loop)
readme.text:
No embeddings, no judge model, no proxy: the "intelligence" is just **acting on evidence the host
already gives you** (a message, an error) instead of asking the model to remember.

- **Stray tools** — a plugin upgrade adds `vendor__new_tool`; if no group matches it, it silently
  becomes visible and burns tokens. `stray` reports visible tools that look like a group's family but
  are matched by nothing (`keep` excluded).
- **Count drift** — `expect` turns "28 hidden" into a checked assertion.
- **Client half not mounted** — `health.client` records the last report from the browser side (`seen` / `at` / `agoSeconds` / which panels). A healthy host does not imply the settings page mounted: on 2026-10-24 all four host contracts were green while the client entry failed to load and the Web UI dropped into recovery mode. This field turns that class of failure into a readable number instead of something you only discover on restart.
- **One bad name in a batch** — if a name in the deny list cannot be restricted, the plugin retries name by name: the rest are still hidden, and the rejected names are recorded (a single bad name no longer voids the whole batch).
- **Zone races** — a sub-agent disposed mid-flight only bumps `stats.restrictSkipped` and does **not**
  count as a failure.
- **Reload orphans** — restriction disposers are owned through `ctx.effect`, so a hot r

```bash
node test/smoke.mjs   # assertions against a fake host, no DSH required (count: use the `node test/smoke.mjs` output)
```

The fake host implements the five contracts this plugin depends on, plus the host's **optional**
`tools.view(scope)` read-only view (the prompt section's main read path; its three degraded shapes —
absent, empty, throwing — each have a test). A contract change breaks the test before it breaks your session.
> Changing this plugin? Read [MAINTAINING.md](MAINTAINING.md) first: any client-side change requires a cold boot, and recovery mode leaves the user unable to operate the UI.

1. **Global tools only.** Tools registered inside an agent scope cannot be hidden — the host rejects it.
2. **Name-based grouping.** DSH's `ToolSchema` has no tags, so groups are globs/regexes over names.
3. **Toggling invalidates the prompt cache.** Enable once and leave it; prefer `only:` when you keep switching.
4. **Auto-collapse only at session start.** It never re-shuffles a running session, because that would
   invalidate the prompt cache mid-task.
5. **Failure mode is fail-open**: if a contract breaks, tools come back and you spend tokens — it will
   not lock you out.
6. **Self-heal only covers tools that exist but are hidden.** A misspelled or not-yet-loaded name
   cannot be repaired; use `lazy_tools_enable { name: "<fragment>" }`.
7. **UI is bilingual, tool descriptions are not.** The settings panel and the composer row follow the
   host locale service; model-facing tool descriptions are registered once at boot and stay in
   Chinese, because the host process has no view of the UI language.

If DSH ever ships native on-demand tool loading (it already carries `deferLoading` and tool-addition
messages), this plugin should retire rather than compete.

Nothing here is a new idea. These are the projects that shaped it — I read 1–3 closely, 4–7 mostly
from their READMEs. If I've mischaracterised yours, open an issue and I'll fix it.

| Project | Layer | What I took / why I diverged |
|---|---|---|
| [tool-attention](https://github.com/asadani/tool-attention) — [arXiv:2604.21816](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21816) | per-turn intent routing over embeddings + two-phase schema loading | established the size of the "tools tax"; I skipped embeddings because a mis-route silently hides a needed tool and the encoder is a large dependency for a token saving |
| [mcp-lazy-load](https://github.com/PeterCha90/mcp-lazy-load) | MCP proxy with `search_tools` / `execute_tool` | shows how far reduction can go; I kept real calls native instead of routing them through a generic executor |
| [dsh-mcp-loader](https://github.com/MikotoMyWife/dsh-mcp-loader) | DSH plugin: per-server loaders + per-agent `restrict` masks | same mechanism layer (it also documents that `restrict` only accepts globally registered names); mine is namespace-agnostic and adds `only:` |
| [lazy-mcp](https://github.com/voicetreelab/lazy-mcp) | proxy layer, tree per server | vocabulary for grouping |
| [opencode-lazy-loading](https://github.com/omarwaly-ai/opencode-lazy-loading) | request-layer stripping | reference for the large-reduction claim |
| [dsh-sieve](h

- **Not a proxy, gateway, or MCP client.** It does not touch transport and adds no hop.
- **Not an auto-router.** It never guesses which tool you meant; you ask, explicitly.
- **Not a security boundary.** A hidden tool is only hidden from the model's tool list — nothing here
  sandboxes or denies execution. Use the host's permission system for that.
